exposure: Vitamin D supplementation (colecalciferol 4000 IU until 16 weeks, then 2000 IU until end of pregnancy)
cohort: The study included 54 pregnant women in their first trimester with 25(OH)D3 deficiency and risk factors for preeclampsia, randomized into two groups.
finding: Supplementation of colecalciferol in addition to a multivitamin-mineral complex throughout pregnancy significantly increased maternal vitamin D levels and was associated with a lower incidence of preeclampsia, premature birth, and fetal growth retardation.
mod_finding: The group receiving additional colecalciferol had a 1.7 times lower incidence of cesarean section compared to the control group.
